claims.text: As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The 13.5% terminal strain reported for HfZrTiTa0.53 is a baseline uniform tensile elongation.
Adding 0.5–1 at.% boron to HfZrTiTa0.53 will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Adding 0.5–1 at.% boron will stabilize grain-boundary phases in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Hot rolling followed by annealing near 600°C and rapid quenching will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Hot rolling can eliminate casting defects and refine grains through dynamic recrystallization, thereby improving ductility.
The proposed boron addition and thermomechanical treatment will enhance dislocation mobility in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The refined grains and stabilized grain-boundary phases will delay crack initiation under tensile loading.
The combined boron and thermomechanical intervention will improve uniform tensile ductility in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The modified alloy will achieve at least 20% uniform tensile elongation.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength above approximately 780 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a compressive strength above 1314 MPa.
The modified HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy will preserve impact-triggered exothermic energy release.
Unmodified HfZrTiTa0.53 has demonstrated impact-triggered chemical energy release similar to tungsten-alloy fragments.
The proposed intervention is expected to remain effective from room temperature to approximately 600°C at a quasi-static tensile strain rate near 10^-4 s^-1.
A thermomechanically processed Zr7 medium-entropy alloy achieved yield strength above 1200 MPa and ductility above 15% after hot rolling, cold rolling, and short annealing.
A fine lamellar dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy retained a combination of tensile strength and ductility at 600°C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats approximately 20% elongation as both the target and a 50% increase over 13.5%, but a 50% increase from 13.5% is 20.25%, so 20.0% does not meet the stated 50% criterion.

The baseline attributes demonstrated energetic performance to HfZrTiTa0.53, whereas the predicted outcome refers to preserving behavior observed in tungsten-alloy fragments; these are different material baselines and are not reconciled.
